pick.name: Langfuse
pick.what: Open-source LLM tracing, prompt management, evals, datasets (OTel-based SDKs)
pick.why: Most adopted OSS option, strong TS SDK (@langfuse/tracing 6.0.2), generous free cloud, self-host for PHI
pick.free_limits: Hobby: 50k units/mo, 30 days data access, 2 users, 30 req/min API. Core $29/mo (100k units, 90 days data access, unlimited users). HIPAA/BAA on Pro ($199/mo) and Enterprise; 50% off first year for early-stage startups
pick.maintained: langfuse py 5.0.4 on 2026-10-21; @langfuse/tracing 6.0.2 on 2026-10-22; acquired by ClickHouse 2026-01-16, MIT core retained

alts.name: Arize Phoenix
alts.what: OTel/OpenInference tracing, evals, datasets, prompt mgmt; pip or single container
alts.why: Lightest self-host, MCP endpoint for Claude Code, strong Python coverage
alts.free_limits: Self-host free; telemetry on by default (PHOENIX_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false)
alts.license: Elastic-2.0 (not OSI open source; cannot offer as managed service)

alts.name: Opik (Comet)
alts.what: Apache-2.0 tracing + evals + pytest integration, Python and TS SDKs
alts.why: Fully Apache-licensed with Docker self-host incl. opik.ps1 for Windows
alts.free_limits: Free tier on cloud/self-host (limits unverified); HIPAA not stated

candidates.name: Langfuse
candidates.verdict: Pick: biggest community, MIT, strong TS

candidates.name: Helicone
candidates.verdict: Reportedly acquired by Mintlify March 2026, maintenance mode (secondary sources); avoid

decision: Langfuse Cloud Hobby for dev; for any PHI or enterprise client self-host it (MIT) because Hobby/Core exclude HIPAA. Move to Phoenix if the ClickHouse stack is too heavy for solo ops, or Opik if you need strictly OSI licences.
details: Retained; ClickHouse acquisition flagged (MIT retained). Supported self-hosted Enterprise reportedly bundled with ClickHouse commercial plans (secondary source). OpenInference: https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference

verify.note: Hobby 50k units, 2 users, 30 req/min; Core $29 (100k, 90 days); Pro $199 with BAA; 50% startup discount year 1 all confirmed. The 30-day figure is data ACCESS per the pricing FAQ, not retention; Core has unlimited users.
